attempts.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (RHEL9, mariadb-server-galera 10.5.29, rsync SST). Firewalld ports 3306/4567(tcp+udp)/4568/4444 opened on all nodes; SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered them. node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster; node2 and node3 joined via systemctl enable --now mariadb. Verified writes through any member are visible on the others. Stopped node3 to prove the cluster stays available (quorum 2/3, Primary, write succeeded); restarted node3 and confirmed automatic IST resync (Synced, size 3) including the row written while it was down. Then ran the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes via systemctl reboot, confirming a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and full Galera recovery (size 3, Primary, Synced, data intact) after each restart before proceeding to the next node.
